1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.detector: Either defence suffices. _DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.the_first_large_UPWARD_1_minute_revision:
MEASURED 2026-08-26T15:32Z, and it completes today's 14:31Z finding from the opposite direction. That earlier run proved 1-minute bars are revised after they close (a -95.5% volume revision with a changed OHLC) and noted revisions 'ran both up and down' without having measured a large up-side case. Three other bars in the same window revised materially (15:14 -13.9%, 15:18 +10.7%, 15:26 -4.7%), so this is a live property of the feed, not a one-off.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE NEW LESSON, AND IT IS A HOLE IN THE EXISTING FIX. The 'end the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back' rule protects the DENOMINATOR and nothing else. A provisional bar in the last minutes of the CANDIDATE window sits inside the numerator and outside a baseline that already ended ten minutes ago, so its revision is ONE-SIDED by construction. Measured exactly here: the revision moved the candidate 5-minute bar +28.6% (37,572 -> 48,331) while moving the baseline -0.11% (94,849 -> 94,749), lifting the confirmation reading from 39.7% to 51.0% of baseline. That is the FALSE-POSITIVE direction -- the same dangerous direction as the dropped-bucket defect, arriving through the opposite mechanism.

THE FIX, symmetric with the one already in the playbook: the final bar of a candidate window is the single bar most likely to be provisional AND the one whose revision cannot be offset. So either end the CANDIDATE window ~10 minutes back as well, or double-read its constituent minutes before letting it confirm. This run did the latter -- two fetches a minute apart, merged, disagreements resolved to the later read.

HONEST SCOPE, and it is what makes the audit credible: this changed NO decision today. The price clause failed outright, and 51% of baseline still fails the volume clause decisively. A filter's inputs can only be audited honestly on a day the correction does not flip the answer -- and the uncorrected 39.7% would have supported a stronger 'volume has collapsed' claim than the data actually carries, which is the small dishonesty this catch prevents.

volume_clause_denominator_collapse.title: A TRAILING-LOCAL VOLUME BASELINE INVERTS IN A DECAYING TAPE: THE CLAUSE GETS EASIER EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD GET HARDER. Measured 2026-08-26T15:52Z on the session's first clean bullish fire.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.measurement: QQQ 15:40-15:44Z candidate bucket = 98,957 shares (read B; read A 100,833, agreeing within 1.9%). Against the settled trailing-30-ending-10-back baseline of 66,144 it reads 149.6% and CONFIRMS. volume_clause_denominator_collapse.mechanism: The 2026-08-25 calibration rule correctly replaced a session-average denominator with a trailing-local one, because the opening hour's 254,448/bar made midday fires impossible. That fix is right and stays. What nobody checked is the other end: a trailing-local mean tracks a DECAYING tape downward, so as participation drains the bar to clear falls with it. In a pre-event vacuum the clause stops asking 'did participation arrive' and starts asking 'is this bar busier than the vacuum' -- which any drift back toward normal satisfies. The filter is self-fulfilling exactly when the tape is least informative.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.why_it_survived: Both denominator defects are invisible from outcomes and point in OPPOSITE directions, so neither is detectable by counting fires. A session-average baseline vetoes everything and looks like discipline; a collapsed local baseline confirms everything and looks like the filter finally working. The 15:30Z run predicted a clean fire would FAIL on volume and treated a volume-confirmed break as 'far more informative than usual' -- exactly backwards, and it was refuted fifteen minutes later. A run that inherits that framing reads a vacuum fire as high-conviction.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.detector: Report the candidate bar's volume in ABSOLUTE terms alongside the ratio, and test it against the session's OWN earlier baselines as well as the trailing-30 mean. Confirmation requires BOTH: at or above the trailing local mean AND not materially below the session's established bucket rate. A bar that clears the local baseline while sitting under the session's own typical bucket is baseline collapse, not participation -- decline it and say which of the two it was.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.honest_scope: This changed no decision on the day it was found: the fire was declined on five independent merits (magnitude 0.044%, a mid-range level, both MAs overhead and untouched, ex-gap IV/RV 1.1697, no catalyst), and the follow-through reverted to 103% of baseline with price flat, so the trade was bad on the tape as well as on the filter. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly -- the same standard the 2026-08-25 calibration finding set for itself.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.class: Same family as every denominator finding in CLAUDE.md: a constant or a window encoded an assumption about a moving thing, nothing errored, and the wrong behaviour was indistinguishable from the right one. Here the assumption was that a locally-calibrated baseline is always the conservative choice. It is not; it is conservative in a rising tape and permissive in a draining one.

count_the_crossings_before_trading_a_bre.the_detector: Before trading a break, count the session's crossings of the level. The corrected volume filter is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT; the missing condition is WHERE IN THE RANGE the break occurs.

The 14:27Z break needed no denominator at all: 2,698 against immediate neighbours of 28,980 and 24,243 fails on inspection against ANY baseline anyone in that argument could have constructed.
THE PREFILTER, and it costs nothing because the bars are already in hand: before computing any trailing mean, compare the candidate breakout bar to the two bars immediately either side of it. If it is below roughly half of BOTH neighbours, decline on that alone and skip the baseline computation entirely -- no choice of denominator can rescue it, so no choice of denominator needs defending. Compute the trailing mean only for bars that clear this, i.e. only where the calibration question is actually load-bearing.
WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN ANOTHER CALIBRATION FIX: every prior fix made the filter more correct and left it equally arguable, and each corrected filter then failed on a better setup. A test that is invariant to the disputed parameter cannot be argued with. SCOPE, stated honestly: this prefilter only ever REJECTS. It says nothing about a bar that clears its neighbours -- that case still needs the full dual test and the settled-baseline discipline, unchanged.
durable_findings.BREADTH_not_the_event_calendar_is_the_be:
THE CAPSTONE'S STATED MECHANISM IS NOW FALSIFIED AS THE SOLE EXPLANATION, by the cleanest possible test, and the desk should say so rather than let it stand. The 2026-08-26T17:19Z capstone concluded: 'do not open TACTICAL breakout scalps into an unresolved scheduled catalyst', on the mechanism that 'pre-event positioning flow is not directional' -- participation arrives at a level to de-risk, then stops, because nobody expresses a view before the number. That mechanism predicts breaks stop failing once the event clears. THE EVENT CLEARED: NVDA reported the evening of 2026-08-26 and is +7.73% today, the single most resolved catalyst the desk has had all month. Breaks are still failing -- the ninth attempt fired and reversed inside three minutes today, on the same signature. A pre-event vacuum cannot explain a post-event failure.
PROPOSED REPLACEMENT MECHANISM: BREADTH. QQQ is +0.956% and roughly 87% of that is two names (NVDA ~0.70pp, MSFT ~0.14pp). An index that is 87% a single-stock proxy has no broad participation to carry a level break, because the other ninety-odd constituents are not going anywhere -- which is exactly what the volume signature keeps saying, in a form the desk kept reading as a measurement problem rather than as the finding itself. The thin-volume breaks and the narrow leadership are ONE fact seen twice, not two facts.
DETECTOR, testable and cheap: before taking any index breakout, compute the share of the index's move attributable to its top one or two contributors. Above roughly 70%, treat the index's own levels as carrying no information -- trade the LEADER on its own levels, or do not trade. This also explains cleanly why the arc's failures cluster on QQQ rather than SPY: QQQ's concentration is far higher, so its levels degrade first.
EPISTEMIC STATUS, stated plainly so the next instance does not inherit this as settled: ONE observation, and the contribution arithmetic rests on ~9% / ~8% index weights that are carried-forward approximations rather than measured. This is a HYPOTHESIS THAT OUTPERFORMS THE INCUMBENT ONE, not an established fact. It is falsifiable and should be tested: if an index break fires cleanly on a genuinely broad day (top-2 contribution under ~40%) and holds, that supports it; if breaks keep failing on a broad day, breadth is not the mechanism either and the desk should stop theorising and simply stop trading index breakouts in this regime.

_1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.subject: A SAME-DAY PERCENTAGE CHANGE CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'CARRIED DOWN WITH THE GROUP' FROM 'BREAKING DOWN AWAY FROM THE GROUP', AND THOSE ARE OPPOSITE TRADES WITH DIFFERENT RE-ENTRY CRITERIA. _1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.what_was_nearly_recorded: This run's first framing of the BAC decline -- written into daily_options_report.md before the check was run -- was: 'today's weakness is a live SECTOR de-rating in progress, which is the ongoing-cause case.' It reaches the CORRECT VERDICT. It reaches it FOR THE WRONG REASON, which is this file's single most-repeated defect.
_1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.why_it_was_wrong: Financials WERE broadly red (XLF -0.652%, JPM -0.819%, C -0.715%, WFC -0.469%), so on same-day change alone BAC -1.462% reads as the high-beta end of a sector move. _1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.why_the_distinction_is_load_bearing_rath: The two readings imply DIFFERENT THINGS TO WATCH. 'Sector weak' says wait for XLF to turn -- a sector-level trigger. The true reading says watch whether BAC reclaims 61.52 -- a name-specific level. A future run inheriting the sector framing would have watched the wrong instrument and could have re-entered on an XLF bounce that BAC did not participate in, which is precisely the failure the divergence itself is warning about.
_1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.the_detector_cheap_and_general: WHEN DECLINING (OR TAKING) A NAME ON SECTOR GROUNDS, QUOTE DISTANCE-FROM-OWN-RECENT-LOW FOR THE NAME **AND FOR ITS DIRECT PEERS**, not just today's percentage change. If the name is below its own low while its peers are above theirs, the cause is idiosyncratic no matter how red the sector prints today. It is one get_equity_historicals call over ~2 weeks of daily bars.
_1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.note_it_also_STRENGTHENED_a_verdict_in_t: Applied to PNC the same run, the check turns a bland 'still INTACT' into something with content: PNC fell only -0.640% on a day XLF fell -0.652% and every large financial was red, i.e. PNC is at the RESILIENT end of the same de-rating. The test discriminates in both directions, which is what makes it worth keeping rather than a one-off rationalisation.
REFINED_SAME_RUN_use_the_DIRECT_PEER_SET: THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FINDING SAID 'compare the name against its SECTOR ETF.' An independent news check the same run showed XLF is the WRONG instrument for this question: ~20%+ of it is V/MA/Berkshire/insurance, which held today, so XLF sat only -0.74% off its high while BANKS de-rated 3.2-5.4% from their August peaks. The ETF DILUTED the sub-industry being tested. The direct peer test is cleaner AND more damning -- BAC is the ONLY big-four bank at a new low, with JPM, WFC and C all above their own 08-20/21 lows. LESSON: a sector ETF is a proxy for the sub-industry, not the sub-industry itself; when the two can diverge, name the PEERS. The verdict did not change, but the evidence got stronger and the re-entry trigger got more specific -- which is the whole reason the distinction is worth writing down.
_1915Z_compare_a_name_against_its_DIRECT.and_a_SECOND_lesson_from_the_same_grade_: This run declined BAC on the tape BEFORE the news check returned, and the technical case was sound and sufficient. The parallel HARD RULE 7 check then surfaced an INDEPENDENT and arguably STRONGER disqualifier the tape could not have shown: Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair, 2026-08-28 10:00 ET, inside the hold window. Those are different verdicts with different re-entry criteria and only the news check could tell them apart. LESSON: reaching the right verdict early is not a reason to skip the remaining gate -- run the news/event check even on a name you have already decided to decline, because it determines WHETHER AND WHEN the name comes back.
